session.name: MPI-539 - a download-mode Pod is a download target, not a generation engine (4 failures, one root, shipped); MPI-540 carded for the toast mess

goal.original: Fabio hit a live incident: connected in download mode (gpu=__cpu__) to install models onto the volume while a local generation ran; every install died, the app dropped to local, and the Model Library was left showing a mix of Pod and local truth. Diagnose and fix.
goal.summary: Root found and fixed: the generation path treated the CPU Pod as its engine. Four failures traced to that one missing concept, all fixed in commit 629ab6cb, suite 555/555 green. The end-to-end proof has NOT been run - Fabio is re-running the exact scenario himself right now (restart, long generation, connect CPU Pod, retry the same downloads). The next session's FIRST job is to read his result, not to re-derive the diagnosis.

completed: ROOT CAUSE, proven from both sides. Pod container log 17:01:37 BST staged loras/krea-2/style/krea2_neondrip.safetensors (469291992 bytes) -> 17:01:39 start-cpu.sh line 69: 21 Killed uvicorn wrapper:app -> 17:01:44 exit code 137 OOM. App log at the SAME instant (app.log is UTC, console is BST): 16:01:39Z hot-store ensure HTTP 502, SSE closed with 4 deps outstanding, 16:01:41Z Remote mode disabled, fell back to local. The CPU Pod has 3.725 GiB RAM. It was serving /health 200 OK two seconds before the stage, and it RESTARTED ITSELF and healed - the app never came back because it had already flipped remote mode off

FIX (the root): getEngine() in js/services/comfyController.js returns the local-pinned engine whenever remoteEngineClient.isDownloadOnly(). _alwaysLocal short-circuits every remote branch, so that one resolution keeps hot-store staging AND the not-ready teardown off the CPU box. isDownloadOnly() already existed from MPI-88, documented as the predicate call sites use to block dispatching a generation - it had exactly ONE consumer, projectUI.js:56, which gates ENTERING a project. Fabio was already inside one, generating, when he connected
FIX: the per-gen engine derivation in js/services/commandExecutor.js (~1255) matches, so the hot-store preflight at ~1505 is not reached in download mode

FIX: _ensureRemoteHotStore guards __cpu__ directly, closing a HALF-WIRE - its stage-on-connect twin prefetchInstalledModels has carried that guard since MPI-329 and the per-gen path never did. Doubly lethal because _remoteVramGb returns null for __cpu__ and null means 'no VRAM cap' in the size filter, so the LEAST capable box got the MOST permissive staging set

FIX: routes/downloadManager.js no longer abandons silently. _failOutstandingRemoteDeps() fails + broadcasts every outstanding dep when remote mode goes inactive, wired into BOTH entry points (the SSE-close path AND the stall watchdog interval, which could previously spin forever when remote went inactive with no stream close to trigger the close path)

TEST tests/download-mode-pod-guards.test.cjs - hits the REAL modules, not a mirrored copy (comfyController imports clean in bare Node; downloadManager was already stubbable, see tests/remote-uninstall-reporting.test.cjs for the harness). MUTATION-CHECKED: removing the getEngine guard fails it with the intended message. Full suite 555/555

IF IT STILL FAILS, the first thing to check is whether /remote/comfy/status returned noGpu at all. The status route only includes noGpu on the branch where /health ANSWERED (routes/remotePodLifecycle.js:646); the 502/booting/dead branches (:637, :639, :653, :655) omit it. The client mirror comes from /remote/mode which always carries it, so getEngine() is safe - but any future guard reading check.noGpu off the STATUS response is not. TOAST MESS - MPI-540, and Fabio explicitly asked for it to be carried here. He has now reported THREE distinct symptoms, only the first of which is root-caused: (a) a stale 'Generation complete / 2 generations finished' OS notification firing ~1h late on the landing page - root-caused, _doneCount in js/shell/notificationService.js:32 is module-level with no expiry and only flushes when generationQueueCount reaches 0, so a count that outlives its batch attaches to a LATER drain; (b) install-toast spam during the agent Pod test runs - NOT reproduced, and note the download:complete handler already filters !data.modelId so the MPI-539 reconcile path (which broadcasts modelId:null) is NOT the source, do not assume it is; (c) 'Not enough disk space to install Boogu Image Edit. Free up space and try again.' - see the next item, this one is NOT purely a toast bug

THE DISK-SPACE TOAST IS TWO PROBLEMS. First, a message-quality bug: routes/downloadManager.js:1688 produces a PRECISE error ('X needed, Y free') and js/services/downloadService.js:234/608/635 replace it with the vague 'Free up space and try again', so the user cannot tell whether the check is right. Boogu Image Edit resolves to 20.8GB (boogu-edit-balanced, 7 deps, computed offline this session); C: has 204GB free and G: has 30GB free, so which root is configured decides whether the check was even correct. Second and more important: FABIO WAS INSTALLING BOOGU ONTO THE POD, NOT LOCALLY - his words, 'I don't have it installed in my system'. So a remote-intended install was evaluated against LOCAL disk. That is the SAME family as MPI-539 failure 4: a queued install carries no engine identity, so it can resume or retry against the wrong engine. Decide whether it belongs on MPI-539 (as the fifth failure of the same root) or its own card BEFORE writing any code

task_card.title: Download-mode Pod is not a generation engine: hot-store OOMs it, the gen preflight kills remote mode, the watchdog is disarmed, and the stranded remote jobs paint over local truth

key_decisions: FIXED THE CONCEPT, NOT THE SYMPTOMS. Three of the four failures were themselves patched fixes with holes: MPI-275's teardown guard (checks connecting, not noGpu), MPI-97's SSE recovery (bails on !isRemoteActive and abandons), MPI-329's staging guard (present on one twin, absent on the other). Adding a fourth guard clause was explicitly rejected - the missing concept was 'a Pod can be a download TARGET without being a generation ENGINE', and routing it at getEngine() is the one place that closes all three

DID NOT flip remoteEngineClient.isRemote() for download-only Pods, even though that looks like the cleaner concept fix. isRemote() has ~30 consumers split across TWO meanings: generation routing AND model-universe scoping. Model scoping MUST stay remote on a download-only Pod - MPI-179 records an LTX Pod install that shipped without its GGUF transformer and read INSTALLED because that mirror was stale false. getEngine() touches only the generation half

The engine string and the engine INSTANCE are separate resolutions (commandExecutor derives 'local'|'remote'; getEngine(forceLocal) picks the object). Both had to be fixed - fixing only the string leaves the dispatch on remoteEngine and the teardown still fires
MPI-540 was split from MPI-539 rather than folded in (the guard-card hook challenges a second card): different module, independent root, no shared code path
